sign.title: Document Signing
sign.subtitle: Sign a document with your Radix wallet. The file never leaves your browser; only its hash is signed.

disclaimer.title: Before you sign
disclaimer.body: Your file is hashed locally and never uploaded. This proves integrity, timestamp and control of your account key, and the disclosed name is self-declared by your wallet, so it is not an identity-verified (qualified) electronic signature. On-chain data is public and permanent: only the hash is anchored, never the file, message or name.

connect.title: Connect your Radix wallet
connect.subtitle: You need a connected wallet to sign a document.

options.onchainMultiNote: On-ledger anchoring becomes available in the result, once everyone has signed.

steps.title: How signing with several people works (off-chain)
steps.s1: You sign the document first and download the certificate (.radixsig.json).
steps.s2: Send that certificate file AND the original document to the other signers.
steps.s3: Each person opens this tool, drops the original file and the certificate under “Co-sign”, and adds their signature.
steps.s4: They send the updated certificate back (or on to the next signer).
steps.s5: When everyone has signed, anyone can anchor it on-ledger from the result screen.
